reasoning: Both sets are rigorous quant plans and both follow the same planning discipline: walk-forward or holdout, purge gaps, per-window PCA fits, null-hypothesis tests corrected per family, and a synthetic M1 walking skeleton. Each also drops something the user explicitly asked for. Set A covers all four stages, with PPO agents, rented-GPU bundles, a hypothesis ledger and a once-only lockbox. But A has no yahooquery cross-check at all, never uses the user's 10 delisted names, and ships no CONSTRAINTS.md even though every context packet and AGENTS.md tell the builder to read it. A also puts RF-03 (tft_targets) on S3/M6 and its milestones are lopsided: M4 bundles the whole shared engine with the covariance study, M3 depends on M2 only to time a page, and M8 bundles forecast portfolios, agents and the verdict. Set B builds the Yahoo cross-check and the 10-name reference check (CHECK-09) into S1 and has a full CONSTRAINTS.md that bans imports from references/. Its milestones are cleaner vertical slices: a synthetic known-answer skeleton per stage, then a real-data milestone. It adds calibration and procedure checks with planted features, which suits a learner. B's own defects are real: it defers PPO agents out of Stage 4 and rules out cloud GPU, falsely claiming 'as the brief requires'. Its brief is still framed for S1 only, its spec is very long, the qdata golden cases TC-74–79 belong to no M1 task, and its M1 packets lack route paths and nested message types. On balance B's plan is more buildable and has fewer missing infrastructure pieces, so it wins narrowly.
